## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1c433b21f90b669ba5134603cf4d8ecaf5451b81`
Local-runs: none
Scope: none + `scripts/pm/fleet-write/execute.mjs`, `scripts/pm/fleet-write/ops.mjs`

Read: card #33768 (body and its 3 comments: triage 6893159294, claim 6897825422, os-dev-report 6898114916; no ruling and no earlier record on the card), PR #34037 (body, file list, net diff against `main` from merge base `c3c0c30d`: 2 files, +24 −15), and the check-runs on the head. `reviewFace` returns no `hits` on the two paths (no published schema, no governed path, no narrowing arm), so the face read off the committed tree is the declaration face; this record was served above it, on the seat's standing practice for `scripts/pm/**`, and reviews both files whole.

Check-runs on the head, snapshot 2026-11-15T17:12Z: 20 completed `success`, 0 failed. Among them every run that judges this diff: `Lint · repo & tooling gates` (it runs `pnpm check:pm-fleet-write-execute`, the executor self-test holding both new pins), `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`. Still in progress at the snapshot, 4: `Test Core (1/8)`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · workspace`. None of the four reads `scripts/pm/fleet-write/**`; the merge gate waits for them regardless, and this verdict does not stand in for them.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`enqueueFrontSizeLift` accept set (ops.mjs) — NARROWED, right.** Before: a carrying `approval_comment` was refused when its first non-empty line was a seat signature. Now: refused when ANY line is one (`body.split(/\r?\n/u)`, the passed-in reader run on each line, the first hit named). Every comment refused before is refused now (the first line is one of the lines); the only newly refused set is "authorised author, on this pull, names the head, a whole-line signature below the first line". No comment that was refused now carries. The PR body's "D3 only refuses more, never widens" holds on the code.
   - Cannot wrongly CARRY a signed one that the old code refused: the reader per line is the same anchored whole-line shape (`SEAT_SIGNATURE_LINE`, trimmed), so a first-line signature reads identically. It newly closes a real shape: a signature that is not the first non-empty line because something precedes it (a carry sentence, or a leading HTML attribution comment line of the kind this very PR body opens with).
   - Cannot wrongly REFUSE beyond the stated rule: a line is a signature only when the WHOLE trimmed line is `LANE#N · ACCOUNT · SESSION`. A blockquoted line (a GitHub quote-reply), a list item, or a signature inside a sentence is not one, so a maintainer quoting a seat's record by hand still carries. A maintainer pasting a seat's signature raw on a line of its own is refused; that is the card's D3 as written, fail-closed, the reading names the signature, and a second comment recovers it.
   - The missing-reader arm is unchanged in effect (`lifts: false`), only its sentence is reworded; a reader that answers null on every line still carries (the existing row holds, CI green).
2. **Refusal reading text — changed, right.** "opens with the seat signature …" becomes "holds the seat signature …"; the tail "a seat's comment is no carried approval" is kept, so the first-line row's pin still matches and the flipped row pins the new head of the sentence. No consumer outside the two files reads either string (surveyed on `main`); `landing-operations.md` L38 says "维护者非席位签名评论", which agrees with both readings.
3. **Self-test roster (execute.mjs) — right.** `pr_dequeue` 28 → 29 with one new row; SIZE lift stays 12 with one row flipped and the battery renamed identically at the roster key and the `battery(...)` call. Total 424 across 31, as the body says; the owning check-run is green.
4. **E2 pin — right, and it pins what the card asks.** Answers `[preflight ok, ok, 502, ok…]`: read-back 1 takes ok then (one poll) 502, pending; one poll; read-back 2 re-reads the queue and takes ok, (one poll), ok. Traced on `dequeueAction` at the head: clock `3 * DEQUEUE_POLL_MS`, 5 pull GETs (1 preflight + 2 + 2), 4 GraphQL calls (preflight queue, mutation, 2 read-backs). The four-number pin separates the three wrong implementations: landing on the failed second read (3000, 3, 3 — the dev's ablation), re-reading the pull once instead of restarting the pair (6000, 4), and restarting the pair without re-reading the queue (GraphQL 3).
5. **E3 jsdocs — right against the code.** `dequeueAction`: "open and unmerged TWICE, one `pollMs` apart — a second read that fails is no confirmation: the queue is read again and the pair starts over" is exactly the loop (`after.pending` falls through to the window check, the sleep, and the next queue read). `dequeuePullAfter`: "ONE of the pull's own GETs … the executor takes TWO such reads, one poll apart, and lands only when both are `ok`" matches the function (one answer in, one verdict out) and its one caller. Both now agree with the file headers.
6. **Public surface — none.** No export added, removed or re-signed; no workflow, schema, skill or governed path in the file list (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green). The relay's envelope (`validate.mjs`) is untouched.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right: the diff is `scripts/pm/fleet-write/**` only and publishes nothing from any released package; `Check Changeset` is green on the head. The body's `Clause-②: no` with no arm is right: the narrowing in ① is of the relay's own accept set, not a published one, so the `(narrowing)` arm is not owed. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing a metadata author writes changes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions`: empty. `deviations`: none declared; none found — the diff stays inside the claim's file surface (the two files, E2, E3, optional D3).
- Flag "D3 taken (optional)": answered — the card offers it, it stays inside the claimed surface, and it narrows only.
- Flag "forced test edit, the 'signature lower down still carries' row flipped": answered — the card's D3 line names that flip itself ("the row pinning … flips with it"); the flipped row asserts the refusal AND the reading, not a weaker pin.
- Flag "concurrency with PR #33975 and PR #34022 on `execute.mjs`": not judged here (their diffs are outside this brief's inputs). ESCALATED to the landing seat: this head reads `blocked`, not conflicting, against `main` today; whichever of the three lands later rebases, and the battery floor (31, or 30 after #34022) is re-read on that rebase.
- `Part of #33768`, open items named honestly: the card has nine boxes; the PR takes E2, E3, D3 and its body names the other six as staying open — the stale `fleet-write.yml` comment and the AGENTS.md (PD#14) sentence (governed, a later batch), N1 and E1 (measured at the first live stroke), D2, D4, N2. Nothing is claimed that the diff does not do, and the card must stay open after the merge with those six unticked.

### ④ Design judgment

No `hits`, so no ④ is owed on this face; the two implementing files are judged against the contract they implement (the card's three items and the file headers): they agree. Findings — must-fix 0, should-fix 0, nit 3:

- **nit 1** `execute.mjs`, the row after the flipped one: its title still says "the opening line unjudged is never a pass" while the reading it guards now says "lines were not judged for a seat signature". Title only; the assertion is unchanged and correct.
- **nit 2** `ops.mjs`, `enqueueFrontSizeLift` jsdoc: `signatureOf` is now handed ONE LINE per call, not the body; the param note still describes it only as "the seat-signature reader". It is right for `readSignatureLine` (a one-line body reads that line); a sentence saying "called once per line" would keep a future reader honest.
- **nit 3** `ops.mjs`, the line split is `\r?\n`, the reader's own. A lone CR (a line ending to the Markdown renderer) is not split, so a signature after one is not read. Not reachable by the writers that sign (they emit LF) and no wider than before this PR; note it on the card only if D3 is ever revisited.
